punchline: Berlekamp sold at six times his price and went back to the university.
thirty_sec: Berkeley professor Elwyn Berlekamp bought the biggest share of Axcom, the firm trading for Medallion, and fixed it: net 55 percent in 1990. About sixteen months after buying he sold to Simons at six times his price, because he preferred academic work to moving to New York.
question: Which part of your daily life would you refuse to trade away, however well a new opportunity paid?
key_contrast: He turned a profit and still chose his own days over staying.
